fig1: From Gaussian scenes to visual localization. Gaussian centers and back-projected rendered depth provide alternative landmark coordinates; multiview triangulation reconstructs coordinates from calibrated feature tracks. Dashed connections identify the alternatives, and the solid connection highlights a track-based correspondence. The lower panels combine query RGB with feature visualization, and query RGB with a render at the estimated pose of the current 3DGS Compact map. The render visualizes alignment and is not part of online localization.
fig2: Overview of AnyGSLoc. A prebuilt Gaussian scene and calibrated reference cameras supply rendered observations for offline map construction; original mapping images are not required. Track-based reconstruction produces the Full map, and localization-aware selection produces the Compact map of 3D coordinates and descriptors. The displayed 3DGS Great Court maps contain 201,063 and 44,631 landmarks, respectively. Online localization globally matches query features to the map and estimates a robust 6-DoF pose in one stage, without rendering.
fig3: Track-based landmark reconstruction. (a) RGB, opacity, and depth guide observation filtering. (b) View-pair matching and depth-guided augmentation provide feature tracks. Both paths apply reciprocal descriptor matching and known-pose epipolar checks; depth restricts the augmentation search. (c) Fixed-camera triangulation determines the landmark coordinates, while view-balanced fusion supplies one descriptor per track. Groups A and B illustrate unequal observation counts. Descriptors are weighted within groups, screened for consistency, and averaged equally across retained groups. The illustrated observations and tracks come from the MAtCha construction evaluated in Table~\ref{tab:t8}.
fig4: Localization-aware landmark selection with the 3DGS Great Court map. Quality pruning retains 37,376 of 201,063 landmarks; coverage completion adds 3,341. Pose-aware completion then adds 4,096 complementary constraints, followed by removal of 182 redundant coverage additions, yielding 44,631 landmarks. The lower panels illustrate the quality factors, reference-view support restoration, and pose complementarity. Candidates C and D are evaluated against the same selected map and reference camera. Dashed and solid contours illustrate uncertainty before and after each addition; relative changes are emphasized for visibility.
e1: Qualitative localization comparison under the protocol of Table~\ref{tab:t4}. STDLoc and ULF-Loc show initial and refined outputs; AnyGSLoc shows the single-stage outputs of Full and Compact. All columns share the query, crop, and vanilla 3DGS rendering model. In each diagonal splice, the upper triangle is rendered at the ground-truth pose and the lower triangle at the estimated pose. Continuity across the marked boundary indicates alignment. Labels give translation error (cm) and rotation error (degrees); the lowest translation error in each row is outlined.
e2: Mapping-view reprojection residuals for the vanilla 3DGS coordinate control in Table~\ref{tab:t5}. The three estimators use the same 1,346,981 observations of 116,303 landmarks in 1,487 reference views of St.~Mary's Church. Gaussian-center and rendered-depth coordinates aggregate their associated proposals; multiview triangulation fits the common observations. Legend values are median residuals. Invalid projections remain in the empirical cumulative distribution denominator. Query-localization accuracy is evaluated separately in Table~\ref{tab:t5}.
e3: Full and Compact maps with matched camera projections and architectural detail crops. Compact displays only retained landmarks. A shared descriptor-PCA transform gives each retained landmark the same color in both maps; the same coloring convention is used in Fig.~\ref{fig:e4}. Each pair uses the same camera, crop, and point size. Complete-map counts include all stored landmarks, while detail counts refer to the outlined regions. Across five scenes, selection reduces 560,996 landmarks to 121,379 (78.36\%).
e4: Gaussian-prior comparison using the Compact configurations in Table~\ref{tab:t8}. Top: prior renderings at the same calibrated camera. PSNR is the scene mean over all registered reference views, rather than the displayed image alone. Middle: Compact maps, with $N$ denoting complete scene-map size. Bottom: ground-truth and estimated-pose renders using the same vanilla 3DGS model per scene and the diagonal convention of Fig.~\ref{fig:e1}. Labels give translation and rotation error; the lowest translation error per scene is outlined. The i3DGS columns show the raw prior and the prior after 1,000 upstream optimization updates. Table~\ref{tab:t8} also reports the Long-LRM conditions.
e5: Localization accuracy and deployment cost on five Cambridge scenes, using the results in Table~\ref{tab:t4}. (a) Cumulative query-core latency to the initial and refined outputs of STDLoc and ULF-Loc; arrows indicate the additional refinement time. Both checkpoints include preceding shared feature computation within the same complete run. Full and Compact each produce a single-stage output. (b) Scene-specific deployment storage summed over five scenes, paired with final-output accuracy. Initial and refined baseline outputs share the same inventory. Horizontal cost axes are logarithmic; recall axes are linear with the displayed panel-specific ranges. Recall and latency are scene-equal means. Timing boundaries and excluded costs follow Sec.~\ref{sec:setup}; complete-frame latency is reported in the supplement.
